title: Role management UI: permission search/filter, templates, and “why was I denied?” messaging
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Background / problem
RBAC v2 introduces a larger, more granular permission set and scoped role bindings (org/project/environment/cluster). During discovery workshops, we repeatedly saw two failures in admin workflows:
1) Admins can’t find the “right” permission among many similarly-named actions, leading to over-granting (“just give them Org Admin”) or support escalations.
2) Users hit 403s and don’t know what to do next. We need a consistent “denied because…” UX (with a safe default for non-admins) that maps to actionable next steps.

This ticket defines the Console UX patterns for:
- Permission search + filtering in role creation/edit flows
- Template selection as a safer default path to least privilege
- Clear, consistent denied messaging across Console surfaces (role management and other Console pages that will be permission-gated)

Goals
- Enable a Security Admin / Org Admin to quickly locate permissions and understand what a permission does, without reading docs.
- Make role templates the primary path for common setups (Org Admin, Security Admin, Billing Admin, Read-only Auditor, Deployment Operator), with transparency into what’s included.
- Provide a consistent permission-denied experience that is:
  - minimally informative to non-admins (avoid enumerating sensitive permissions)
  - more informative to admins (including reason codes and troubleshooting pointers)
  - consistent across Console routes
- Ensure patterns work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments where scope is critical (org vs project vs environment/cluster).

Non-goals
- Full custom policy authoring (ABAC / rule scripting)
- Redesign of identity (SSO/SAML login and group sync remain separate)
- Final taxonomy decisions for every permission string (covered by ADR-014 and permission catalog work); we design for discoverability and clarity given those strings

Primary personas
- Security Admin (enterprise): manages least-privilege roles, audit exports, retention controls, break-glass procedures
- Platform Operator (private/dedicated): manages deployments, routing policies, model pinning/rollouts, incident response
- Read-only Auditor: needs evidence and auditability without ability to change production settings

Entry points / information architecture
1) Console → Settings → Access control → Roles
   - Roles list
   - Create role (from template OR custom)
   - Role detail view (members/bindings, permissions summary)
   - Edit role (permissions)

2) Console surfaces that can yield a permission denial
   - Access control pages themselves (meta: you can be denied from managing roles)
   - Audit logs export
   - Routing policy editor / rollout controls
   - API key management

Design: Permission search & filter
Where it appears
- Role create/edit screen, in a dedicated “Permissions” step or side panel.
- Template inspection view (read-only) uses the same permission list component.

Core behaviors
- Search field filters the permission list live (client-side filter of loaded permission catalog). Search matches:
  - permission ID string (e.g., routing.policy.update)
  - display name (humanized)
  - description text
  - resource type keywords (e.g., “audit”, “api key”, “deployment”, “routing”, “retention”)
- Filters (chips) narrow by:
  - Product area: Access control, API keys, Deployments, Routing, Models & rollouts, Audit logs, Billing
  - Sensitivity tier (if available from catalog metadata): Low / Medium / High / Break-glass
  - Applicability: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (for Private-heavy roles)
- Sorting:
  - Default: grouped by product area, then alphabetical by display name
  - Option: “Show selected first” toggle (sticky) to reduce review errors

Permission list item anatomy
- Display name (short, human readable)
- Permission ID (monospace, secondary)
- One-line description (“Allows exporting audit logs for an org to configured sinks.”)
- “Risk badge” / sensitivity tag (e.g., High) to encourage review
- Optional “Scope notes” line for scope-sensitive permissions (e.g., “Applies at Project or Environment scope”)—content comes from metadata if available

Selection and bulk actions
- Single checkbox per permission
- Group header supports “Select all in group” (with a confirmation if group contains High/Break-glass)
- Bulk actions in header when selections exist:
  - “Remove selected”
  - “Export selected as JSON” (admin convenience for internal review; can be hidden behind internal feature flag if needed)

Empty states
- No matches: “No permissions match ‘{query}’. Try searching for an object (audit, key, routing) or an action (read, update, export).”
- Permission catalog not loaded: show skeleton and retry; do not allow saving role with partial catalog.

Guardrails
- If user includes any Break-glass-tagged permission, show inline warning:
  - “This permission is intended for emergency access workflows. Confirm you understand the monitoring and approvals requirements.”
  - Require explicit acknowledgement checkbox before saving.

Design: Template selection
Rationale
Most customers want a small number of standard roles with known semantics. Templates reduce misconfiguration and speed adoption for Private/Dedicated pilots.

Flow
- Create role entry screen offers two primary choices:
  1) “Start from template” (recommended)
  2) “Start from scratch” (secondary)

Template browser
- Template cards show:
  - Role name (e.g., Read-only Auditor)
  - Short description (“View audit logs and compliance settings without edit access.”)
  - Intended scope(s): Org / Project / Environment / Cluster
  - “Common for”: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
- Clicking a template opens a preview drawer:
  - Permissions included (same permission list component; read-only)
  - Default scope recommendation (e.g., “Bind at Org scope”)
  - Notes (e.g., “Does not include key rotation by default”)

Customization
- After choosing a template, user lands in role editor with permissions pre-selected.
- Editor should show a “Modified from template” indicator once permissions diverge.
- Provide “Reset to template” action.

Design: Denied messaging (“Why was I denied?”)
Principles
- Safe by default: do not leak sensitive permission names to unauthorized users.
- Actionable: give next steps (request access, contact admin, view required role).
- Consistent: same structure/copy across Console pages.
- Traceable: for admins, include correlation ID + optional debug details.

Error states
A) Non-admin / standard user (default)
- Title: “You don’t have access to this action”
- Body: “Your account is missing the required permissions to continue.”
- Actions:
  - “Request access” (opens modal with pre-filled message including page/action and timestamp)
  - “Switch org/project” if applicable
- Footer: “Reference ID: {request_id}” for support.

B) Admin (or users with a specific “view authz debug” permission)
- Title: “Access denied”
- Body includes:
  - Required permission(s) (display name + ID)
  - Scope evaluated (org/project/env/cluster identifier)
  - Denial reason code (from backend; user-readable label)
  - “Policy version” / “role bindings considered” if provided
- Actions:
  - “Manage roles” (deep link to roles page with user pre-filtered)
  - “View audit event” (if denial is logged and user can view audit logs)

Denial reason codes (UX mapping)
We align UI copy with reason codes coming from platform (see ENG work on standardized codes). Proposed mapping:
- MISSING_PERMISSION → “Missing permission” + show required permission(s) (admin only)
- SCOPE_MISMATCH → “Access exists, but at a different scope” + suggest where to bind role
- EXPLICIT_DENY → “Blocked by policy” (admin only; do not expose details to standard users)
- POLICY_NOT_FOUND / STALE_CACHE → “Authorization system error” + retry guidance + support link

Placement and components
- In-page permission denied (preferred) for actions initiated inside a page (e.g., export button). Use inline callout near control.
- Full-page 403 for navigation to restricted page.
- Toast is insufficient alone; can be additive but must not be the only signal.

Copy specifics (MVP)
- Keep “permission” wording; avoid “role” wording in the first line because user may have multiple roles.
- Use “contact your org admin” phrasing; for Private deployments allow customization to “contact your platform admin”.

Accessibility
- Search and filters must be keyboard navigable (tab order: search → filter chips → list items)
- Permission list must announce selection changes (ARIA live region) and preserve scroll position when selecting.
- Denied pages must have clear heading structure and not rely solely on color.

Instrumentation (for success metrics)
- Track:
  - permission_search_used (query length bucketed, not raw text by default; raw text gated behind internal/dev setting due to potential sensitive strings)
  - template_selected (template name)
  - template_modified (boolean)
  - permission_denied_shown (reason code, surface, admin_debug_enabled)
- These support PM success metrics: reduction in support tickets and faster role setup.

Open questions
- Do we need a dedicated permission “view authz debug details” or can this be granted implicitly to Security Admin? (Security preference: explicit permission.)
- How should we display environment/cluster scope in Private deployments where identifiers may be customer-defined and sometimes opaque?
- Should “Request access” integrate with JIRA/ServiceNow for enterprise accounts, or start with copy-to-clipboard/email?

Acceptance criteria
- Role editor includes search, product-area filters, sensitivity filter, and “show selected first” toggle.
- Templates can be previewed and selected; template-derived roles clearly indicate divergence.
- Console shows consistent denied UX across at least: role management, audit export, and routing policy edit flows.
- Admin debug view is only accessible when authorized; non-admin view reveals no permission IDs.

Handoff notes
- Components to build:
  - PermissionPicker (search + filters + list + selection)
  - TemplateBrowser + TemplatePreviewDrawer
  - DeniedState (inline + full-page variants)
- Content dependencies:
  - Permission catalog metadata must include: display_name, description, product_area, sensitivity, and (ideally) scope_notes.
  - Backend should provide: request_id, reason_code, required_permissions[], evaluated_scope.

Links
- Confluence: Console role management UX spec (draft) — sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-role-management-ux.json
- Linear: DES-927 (Denied error states + copy), PM-661 (Scope definition)

Next steps
- Finalize component behavior with Console engineering (Chloe/Felix) and confirm what authz debug fields will be available.
- Run a quick usability pass with 2–3 internal admins (IT + Security Eng) focusing on finding permissions and understanding denials.
- Ensure design tokens for risk/sensitivity badges align with existing Console badge styles.
comments: 2025-02-03 — Naomi Feldman (PM): Please ensure templates are the default path in MVP. We’re seeing Private prospects ask for ‘auditor’ and ‘deployment operator’ roles by name; make those easy to find and explain.

2025-02-05 — Felix Schneider (Console eng): Backend can return request_id and reason_code; required_permissions[] is planned but might not be in first cut. Suggest design a progressive disclosure where admin view can show ‘Required permissions unavailable’ gracefully.

2025-02-06 — Marcus Lin (Security Eng): +1 to not exposing permission IDs to non-admins. For admin view, OK to show permission IDs but avoid listing all considered role bindings unless explicitly enabled (could leak org structure).

2025-02-10 — David Kim (IT/Identity): For “Request access”, internal users will expect Slack or ticket integration. For MVP, a copy-to-clipboard message that includes org/project and the Reference ID is fine; we can document internal workflow.

2025-02-12 — Tessa Morgan (Design): Updated denied patterns to include two-tier disclosure (standard vs admin-debug). Added ‘scope mismatch’ case explicitly; this came up in scope thread and Private POC notes.
